meanings.note: Colloquial. Common masculine noun meaning 'mess, chaos' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We have a bit of a mess here.
There was total chaos in the room.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'name badge' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ты уволена. Рот закрой и бейджик сдай.
examples.trans: You are fired. Shut your mouth and hand in your badge.

examples.text: На кухне ресторана всегда есть бейджик.
examples.trans: In the restaurant kitchen there is always name badge.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Who are your rivals?
Is this your programme?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: For emphasis.

examples.trans: That's no problem at all.
I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: Проводить время = to spend time. Common neuter noun meaning 'time' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I don't have time.
We're having a good time.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.
She's always like that.
There's always a way out.
She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.en: to recall, to try to remember, to reminisce
meanings.note: Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'поминать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to recall, to remember', paired with 'вспомнить'.

examples.trans: I'm trying to recall it.

examples.text: Я так вспоминаю. Значит, машину разбил, что ли?
examples.trans: I'm trying to recall it. So I wrecked the car, then?
I am just recalling old stories.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Come on, everything is fine.
Come on, that is all.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: As you all know...
Does the governor support you?

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: выбирать слова = to choose one's words

examples.trans: He takes a long time choosing a new dish.
Always choose the right words.

examples.text: Выбирай слова, когда говоришь с ней!
examples.trans: Choose your words when talking with her!

meanings.note: The plural 'выборы'. Common masculine noun meaning 'choice' in everyday Russian.
The plural 'выборы'. Common masculine noun meaning 'choice' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: We have no choice.
It's your choice.
Marina, we have no choice.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: He talks for a long time.
I waited a long time.
We'll make it! The president always talks for a long time.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'value, treasure'.

examples.trans: Do you value your reputation at all?

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и дорожить вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and value on time.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: That's life.
I want a different life.
Working. Making people's lives better.

meanings.note: A door, a shop, or a legal case. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крыть'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to close, to shut', paired with 'закрывать'.

examples.trans: We will close your case.
Close the door, please.

examples.text: А потом, Аркадий Борисович, мы закроем ваше дело.
examples.trans: And then, Arkady Borisovich, we will close your case.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'apologize'.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и извиняться вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and apologize on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют извиняться.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to apologize.

meanings.note: Core Russian conj meaning 'or' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Or even better.
Tea or coffee?
Or even better: a spa!

meanings.note: declines like какой: какая-то, какое-то, какие-то

examples.trans: What nonsense.
Some man called you.

examples.text: Бред какой-то. Но, с другой стороны, чем я рискую?
examples.trans: What nonsense. But on the other hand, what have I got to lose?

meanings.note: joins a description to a noun; agrees with that noun in gender and number

examples.trans: This is a mayor who keeps his word.
Where is the book that was here?

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: No, it's mine.
No? All right.
No. That's mine.

meanings.note: Colloquial. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
How are you? — OK.
Good! Everything's fine over there.

meanings.note: hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Oh, come on, Dad!
Well?

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.trans: I'm thinking about it.
We're talking about the town.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'served'.

examples.trans: She is the one who served me.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и обслуживать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and served on time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'об-' ('around, about') marks encirclement or comprehensive action (stem 'считать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to shortchange, overcharge'.

examples.text: И начинай скандал, будто тебя хотят обсчитать.
examples.trans: And start a scandal, as if they want to overcharge you.

examples.text: Это нормально? Ваш официант хотел меня обсчитать!
examples.trans: Is this normal? Your waiter wanted to overcharge me!
Did something happen? They tried to overcharge me.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: From German 'Offiziant' / Late Latin 'officians' (one who performs a duty or service).

examples.trans: The waiter politely greets the new guests.
Please do not block the walkway for the waiters.
To command the waiters.

meanings.note: Сделать ошибку = to make a mistake. Common feminine noun meaning 'mistake, error' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: There are many serious mistakes in the case.
That is my mistake.

examples.text: А прокуратура думает иначе. В деле много грубых ошибок.
examples.trans: The prosecutor's office thinks otherwise. There are many serious mistakes in the case.

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ставить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'framed / set up'.

examples.trans: I swear, they simply framed me.
They simply framed me!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.trans: Show me your hands!
Shall we show this to Anikeev?

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?

meanings.note: as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine
as a side word: Правда, всё нормально = Honestly, everything's fine

examples.trans: Honestly, everything's fine.
That's true.

examples.text: Правда, Нин, всё нормально. Скажи что-нибудь, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Honestly, Nina, everything's fine. Say something, please.

meanings.note: Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn into, to transform', paired with 'превращать'.

examples.text: Они умеют превратить работу в праздник.
examples.trans: They know how to turn work into a holiday.

examples.text: Дети умеют превратить работу в праздник.
examples.trans: Children know how to turn work into a holiday.

examples.text: Вы хотите превратить её в чёрную?
examples.trans: Do you want to turn it into black?

meanings.note: usually 3rd person: что произошло? = what happened?

examples.trans: What happened?

examples.text: Я не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: I don't know how it happened.

examples.text: Николай Филиппович, простите меня, пожалуйста. Я сам не знаю, как это произошло.
examples.trans: Nikolai Filippovich, please forgive me. I don't know myself how it happened.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'молчать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to then'.

examples.text: Подожди, а почему ты тогда промолчал?
examples.trans: Wait, and why did you stay silent then?

examples.text: Лев, сегодня вам ещё есть чему учиться.
examples.trans: Lev, today showed you still have much to learn.

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to ask (for)', paired with 'попросить'.

examples.trans: I apologise.
He's asking for help.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.note: 'это просто' = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Это просто = it's easy. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I'm just tired.
It's easy.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: просить прощения = to ask for forgiveness, apologise

examples.trans: I apologise.
He is asking me to forgive him.

examples.text: Когда вырасту, ты будешь просить у меня прощения!
examples.trans: When I grow up, you'll be begging me to forgive you!

meanings.en: to try, to attempt, to make an effort
meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to try, to attempt', paired with 'попытаться'.

examples.trans: I tried!
He tried to explain the situation.

examples.text: Пыталась? С бутылкой вина в руке?
examples.trans: You tried? With a bottle of wine in your hand?

разобраться.gloss: to sort out, to figure out

meanings.en: to sort out, to settle, to deal with
meanings.note: мы сами разберёмся = we'll sort it out ourselves

В + prepositional. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to sort out, to figure out', paired with 'разбираться'.

examples.text: Аникеев, иди к себе, а мы разберёмся.
examples.trans: Anikeev, go to your room, and we'll sort this out.
I'll figure everything out soon.

examples.text: Ну да, это понятно. Потом разберёмся.
examples.trans: Well yes, that's understandable. We'll sort it out later.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'result' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я жду только одного — результатов от вас.
examples.trans: I expect only one thing: results from you.
This is an excellent result of the work.

examples.text: Я жду только одного — результатов от вас. Работайте!
examples.trans: I expect only one thing: results from you. Get to work!

meanings.note: From French 'réputation' / Latin 'reputatio' (consideration, public standing).

examples.text: У меня репутация, я не проигрываю.
examples.trans: I have a reputation, I don't lose.
He has an excellent reputation.

examples.text: У меня репутация, я не проигрываю. У твоего Самсонова шансов нет.
examples.trans: I have a reputation, I don't lose. Your Samsonov has no chance.

meanings.note: fleeting vowel о drops in oblique cases: рта, рту, ртом; locative во рту

examples.trans: Samsonov, shut your mouth!
Open your mouth and say 'ah'.

examples.text: Самсонов, рот закрой! Зачем ты его обижаешь?
examples.trans: Samsonov, shut your mouth! Why are you insulting him?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.trans: He keeps his word.
They are building their houses.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

сдать.gloss: to return, to hand in; to pass (an exam)

meanings.en: to return, to hand back, to turn in
meanings.note: A rented car, key, or ticket. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'дать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to return, to hand in; to pass (an exam)', paired with 'сдавать'.

An exam: сдать экзамен. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'дать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to return, to hand in; to pass (an exam)', paired with 'сдавать'.

examples.text: Нам надо сдать машину до десяти часов.
examples.trans: We have to return the car before ten o'clock.
I passed all my exams.

examples.text: Я за комнаткой пригляжу. Может, сдам кому, а денежки пополам!
examples.trans: I'll look after the little room. Maybe I'll rent it to someone, and we'll split the money!

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to say, to tell', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.trans: What did you say?
Excuse me, where's the metro?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('fired, dismissed').

examples.trans: You are all fired.

examples.text: Ты не уволена, я просто пошутила.
examples.trans: You are not fired, I was simply joking.

meanings.note: Уволен = fired (short participle). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to fire, to dismiss', paired with 'увольнять'.

examples.trans: You're fired!
He was fired.

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'owner', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The restaurant owner personally greets the guests.
The owner is busy in the kitchen for now.

examples.text: Вовсе нет, я жду хозяина ресторана.
examples.trans: Not at all, I am waiting for the restaurant owner.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: I want coffee.
If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'something; somehow', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Did something happen?
Has something happened?
Somehow I'm tired.

meanings.note: Без шуток = seriously. Common feminine noun meaning 'joke' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It's a joke.
What kind of jokes are these?
Normal jokes. Where's the money?

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
